subsystems.name: Rotor (inner loop)
subsystems.role: a continuous cable or chain of linked masses that circulates faster than orbital speed, creating outward force that supports the ring.

subsystems.name: Stationary ring (stator)
subsystems.role: the outer shell that rides on the rotor's magnetic field; carries platforms, launchers and habitats.

subsystems.name: Magnetic levitation and drive
subsystems.role: keeps the rotor moving and transfers momentum between rotor and ring.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: supplies the energy to spin up the rotor and make up losses.

subsystems.name: Tethers and anchors
subsystems.role: optional links to the planet's surface that stabilize the ring and allow payload transfer.

subsystems.name: Control and stabilization
subsystems.role: actively maintains the ring's shape and position against perturbations.

buildSteps.title: Concept and simulation
buildSteps.detail: Model the dynamics of a rotating ring and its magnetic coupling; design control laws for stability.

buildSteps.title: Material and component testing
buildSteps.detail: Test cables, magnets and bearings in vacuum and thermal cycling to qualify them for space.

buildSteps.title: In-orbit assembly infrastructure
buildSteps.detail: Establish robotic assembly and manufacturing in low Earth orbit to build large structures from launched modules.

buildSteps.title: Launch and deploy rotor segments
buildSteps.detail: Send up many payloads of rotor cable or linked segments and assemble them into a continuous loop.

buildSteps.title: Spin up the rotor
buildSteps.detail: Use ground-based or space-based electromagnetic launchers to accelerate the rotor to above orbital velocity.

buildSteps.title: Lift and stabilize the stationary ring
buildSteps.detail: As rotor speed increases, magnetic forces lift the stator; active control holds it in place.

buildSteps.title: Attach tethers and platforms
buildSteps.detail: Lower tethers to the surface and build launch loops, docking ports and transit stations.

buildSteps.title: Commission and operate
buildSteps.detail: Test payload transfer and launch; operate as infrastructure for space access and planetary transit.

prerequisites.why: efficient magnetic levitation and coupling at scale require superconductors that work in space conditions.
the ring must be built from many pieces launched from Earth, requiring robotic assembly at unprecedented scale.
thousands of tonnes of material must be lifted to orbit; current launch costs are too high.
no existing system controls a structure thousands of kilometres long with the required precision.
spinning up and maintaining the rotor consumes enormous energy.

pathway.milestone: small-scale demonstrations of magnetic levitation and active mass drivers in vacuum
in-orbit robotic assembly of a hundreds-of-metres truss
pathway.unlocks: experience with building large structures in space.

pathway.milestone: a sub-scale orbital ring segment in low Earth orbit
pathway.unlocks: proves the dynamics of a rotating, actively supported ring.
non-rocket launch and rapid global transit.
